quick.summary: Why a dashboard nobody opens fails, and three rules for one they will.
quick.takeaway: One question per chart. Few numbers. Honest axes.

beats.line: I built a dashboard with thirty charts. Why does nobody open it?
Then it answers none at a glance. Three rules.
First, each chart answers one question, written as its title.
Second, keep the few numbers the team acts on.
Third, bar charts start at zero, so sizes look honest.
But more charts give people more answers?
More charts give them more searching. Answers come from fewer.
Five charts. Each title asks what the team checks on Monday.

quiz.question: What makes a dashboard chart easiest to read at a glance?
options: A title stating the one question it answers
Many metrics on the same chart
An axis that starts near the data
quiz.explanation: A chart built around one question tells the reader what to look for straight away.

quiz.question: Adding more charts to a dashboard usually makes it more useful.
quiz.explanation: More charts make people search. A few charts that answer the team’s regular questions get used.
